text:
The Indian equity market closed the week modestly higher. The Nifty 50 finished at 25,607, up 0.36%, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 0.22% to 23,949. The Bank Nifty slipped marginally, down 0.04% to 63,041. Volatility edged up, with the India VIX at 16.55 (+2.70%). Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) continued a long buying streak – net purchases of INR 27,938 crore for the 21st session – while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) added INR 1,473 crore after a single day of net selling. Breadth was healthy (score 62.7), with 64.7% of stocks above their 20‑day average and 17 new 52‑week highs versus only three lows.

In IPO activity, Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) Limited opened on 26 Nov and will close on 30 Nov, priced at INR 181‑191 with a fresh‑plus‑OFS structure; total subscription was 1.47 times. Recent listings showed mixed performance: Mahanadi Coalfields listed at INR 136 and fell 2.6% from issue, while Crystal Crop Protection opened at INR 272, rose 2.2% on day one but is now down 3.2% from issue. Upcoming offerings next week include Matangi Rubber (price band INR 163‑172), Monomark Engineering (INR 60‑65) and Swara Baby Products (INR 105‑111), all fresh or fresh + OFS issues.

Key catalysts for the coming week are global and domestic cues. The USD‑INR eased to 92.98 (‑0.34%), Brent crude slipped to $91.19 (‑0.86%) and gold fell to $3,663.7 (‑0.59%), easing commodity‑price pressure. However, the S&P 500 futures rose 0.83% and the Nasdaq fell 0.84%, indicating mixed US market sentiment. Domestic headlines point to profit‑booking after a four‑week rally and a possible slowdown in the IT and financial sectors, which have been weighing on the Nifty. Investors should watch RBI policy moves, crude price trends and any fresh foreign inflows as they could sway market direction.
